s: Mahavira, born Vardhamana, was a religious reformer and spiritual leader, considered by Jains to be the 24th and final Tirthankara. By traditional accounts he was born in 599 BCE into a ruling family.
k: Mahavira was a great teacher of the Jain religion. Jains count him as the last of 24 great teachers. Tradition says he was born a prince in 599 BCE.

s: Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, was a wandering religious teacher who lived in the eastern Indo-Gangetic Plains in the 6th or 5th century BCE. According to Buddhist legends he was born at Lumbini, in what is now Nepal, to royal parents of the Shakya clan, and gave up his home life.
k: The Buddha was a teacher who lived about 2,500 years ago. Stories say he was born a prince at Lumbini, in today's Nepal, and gave up his rich life to search for the truth. Buddhism is the religion that follows his teaching.

s: Panini was an ancient Sanskrit grammarian and linguist. His masterwork, the Ashtadhyayi, dated somewhere between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE, is the foundational text of the Indian science of grammar.
k: Panini was a scholar who worked out the rules of the Sanskrit language and wrote them down in a famous book.

s: Chanakya, according to legendary narratives preserved from the 4th to the 11th century CE, was a Brahmin who assisted the first Mauryan emperor, Chandragupta.
k: Old stories say that a clever teacher named Chanakya helped Chandragupta Maurya to win his empire.

s: Thiruvalluvar was a philosopher and Tamil-language poet of the post-Sangam era, best known as the author of the Tirukkural, a collection of couplets. His lifetime has been dated variously from the fourth century BCE to the early fifth century CE.
k: Thiruvalluvar was a Tamil poet and thinker. He wrote the Kural, a famous book of very short poems about how to live well. Nobody is sure exactly when he lived.

s: Chandragupta Maurya, who reigned from about 320 to 298 BCE, was the founder and first emperor of the Maurya Empire, based in Magadha.
k: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire about 2,300 years ago and was its first emperor.

s: Ashoka, known as Ashoka the Great, was Emperor of Magadha from about 268 BCE until his death in 232 BCE, and the third ruler of the Maurya Empire.
k: Ashoka was the third emperor of the Maurya family and ruled most of India. He had his messages carved on rocks and pillars across the land.

s: Avvaiyar was a Tamil poet who lived during the Sangam period. She wrote 59 poems in the anthology Purananuru.
k: Avvaiyar was a Tamil woman poet who lived about 2,000 years ago. Fifty-nine of her poems survive in one old collection.

s: Kharavela was the emperor of Kalinga in the 2nd or 1st century BC. The main source for his life is his rock-cut Hathigumpha inscription, which is undated.
k: Kharavela was a king of Kalinga, in today's Odisha. Almost everything we know about him comes from one long message carved in a cave.

s: Kanishka I, known as Kanishka the Great, was an emperor of the Kushan dynasty, reigning about 127 to 150 CE. Under him the empire reached its zenith.
k: Kanishka was the greatest emperor of the Kushans. He ruled about 1,900 years ago.

s: Nagarjuna, about 150 to 250 CE, was a scholar-monk, philosopher and teacher of Mahayana Buddhism from southern India. He is considered the founder of the Madhyamaka school.
k: Nagarjuna was a Buddhist monk and deep thinker from southern India who lived about 1,800 years ago.

s: Samudragupta was the second emperor of the Gupta Empire, a son of the emperor Chandragupta I and the Licchavi princess Kumaradevi.
k: Samudragupta was the second emperor of the Gupta family. His mother was a princess of the Licchavi clan.

s: Faxian was a Chinese Buddhist monk and translator who travelled on foot to classical India to acquire Buddhist texts.
k: Faxian was a Buddhist monk who walked all the way from China to India to collect holy books.

s: Kalidasa was a Classical Sanskrit author often considered ancient India's greatest poet and playwright. He is often placed in the 4th century CE, though his dates are uncertain.
k: Kalidasa wrote plays and poems in Sanskrit about 1,600 years ago. Many people think he was the greatest poet of ancient India.

s: Bodhidharma was a semi-legendary Buddhist monk who lived during the 5th or 6th century CE. He is traditionally credited with bringing Chan Buddhism to China.
k: Bodhidharma was a Buddhist monk who, the stories say, travelled to China and began the kind of Buddhism known as Chan, or Zen.

s: Aryabhata was the first of the major mathematician-astronomers of the classical age of Indian mathematics and astronomy. His works include the Aryabhatiya, which mentions that in 499 CE he was 23 years old.
k: Aryabhata was a great mathematician and astronomer. He wrote his famous book when he was only 23 years old.

s: Varahamihira was an ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer who lived in Ujjain, in the Avanti region of today's Madhya Pradesh.
k: Varahamihira was an astronomer who lived in the city of Ujjain about 1,500 years ago.

s: Brahmagupta, born at Bhillamala, today's Bhinmal in Rajasthan, was a mathematician and astronomer credited as the first person to understand and formalise the concept of zero as a number. His Brahmasphutasiddhanta is dated 628.
k: Brahmagupta was a mathematician born in Rajasthan. He was the first to write down rules for doing sums with zero.

s: Xuanzang, born near present-day Luoyang in China on 6 April 602, was a 7th-century Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveller and translator.
k: Xuanzang was a Buddhist monk, scholar and traveller from China who lived about 1,400 years ago.

s: Pulakeshin II was the Chalukya emperor from about 609 to 642. During his reign the Chalukya empire of Vatapi expanded to cover most of the Deccan.
k: Pulakeshin was a Chalukya king who ruled most of the Deccan about 1,400 years ago.

s: Adi Shankara was a Vedic scholar-monk, philosopher and teacher of Advaita Vedanta, who wrote influential commentaries. Scholars place him in the first half of the 8th century CE, though tradition gives a much earlier date.
k: Adi Shankara was a wandering monk and thinker who lived about 1,300 years ago. He taught a philosophy called Advaita Vedanta.

s: Andal, also known as Kodhai, is one of the 12 Alvars, the Tamil poet-saints of the Bhakti movement, and the only woman among them. Active in the eighth century CE, she is credited with the Tamil works Tiruppavai and Nachiyar Tirumoli.
k: Andal was a Tamil poet and saint who lived about 1,300 years ago. She is the only woman among twelve famous poet-saints, and her songs are still sung.

s: Rajaraja I, known as Rajaraja the Great, was a Chola emperor who reigned from 985 to 1014, known for his conquests in southern India and Sri Lanka.
k: Rajaraja was a great Chola emperor. He conquered much of southern India and built the giant temple at Thanjavur.

s: Rajendra I, often called Rajendra the Great, was a Chola emperor who reigned from 1014 to 1044. He was born in Thanjavur, the son of Rajaraja I.
k: Rajendra was the son of Rajaraja and the next Chola emperor. His ships sailed as far as Southeast Asia.

s: Atisha Dipamkara Shrijnana was a Buddhist religious teacher and leader from Bengal, generally associated with the works he wrote at the Vikramashila monastery.
k: Atisha was a Buddhist teacher from Bengal who lived about a thousand years ago.

s: Ramanuja was a Hindu philosopher, guru and social reformer, one of the most important exponents of the Sri Vaishnavism tradition.
k: Ramanuja was a Hindu teacher and thinker who lived about 900 years ago.

s: Bhaskara II, known as Bhaskaracharya, was a polymath, mathematician and astronomer whose works represent the high point of the classical Siddhanta school. He was born in 1114.
k: Bhaskara was one of India's greatest mathematicians and astronomers. He was born in 1114.

s: Akka Mahadevi was a 12th-century philosopher, poet and mystic, and a prominent member of the Lingayat movement. Some 430 of her short poems, called vachanas, are known.
k: Akka Mahadevi was a poet and saint who lived about 850 years ago. She left about 430 short poems.

s: Mu'in al-Din Chishti, known as Khawaja Gharib Nawaz, was a Persian Islamic scholar and mystic from Sistan who eventually settled in the Indian subcontinent. His shrine is at Ajmer.
k: Moinuddin Chishti was a Sufi holy man who came to India from Persia about 800 years ago. His tomb is at Ajmer.

s: Nizamuddin Auliya was a Sufi saint. His dargah, a shrine and mosque complex, stands in the Nizamuddin area of Delhi.
k: Nizamuddin Auliya was a Sufi saint who lived about 700 years ago. His tomb in Delhi is a famous shrine.

s: Dnyaneshwar, also called Jnaneshwar, was a 13th-century Marathi saint, poet and philosopher.
k: Dnyaneshwar was a saint and poet of Maharashtra who lived about 750 years ago.

s: Amir Khusrau was an Indo-Persian Sufi singer, musician and court poet of the Delhi Sultanate.
k: Amir Khusrau was a poet and musician at the court of the sultans of Delhi about 700 years ago.

s: Alauddin Khalji was Sultan of Delhi, of the Khalji dynasty, from 1296 until his death in 1316.
k: Alauddin Khalji was a powerful sultan of Delhi from 1296 to 1316.

s: Muhammad bin Tughluq was a Sultan of Delhi, also known by the epithets "the Eccentric Prince" and "the Mad Sultan".
k: Muhammad bin Tughluq was a sultan of Delhi about 700 years ago. He was nicknamed the Eccentric Prince and the Mad Sultan.

s: Lalleshwari, commonly known as Lal Ded, was a Kashmiri mystic of the Kashmir Shaivism school and the creator of a style of mystic poetry.
k: Lal Ded was a holy woman and poet of Kashmir who lived about 650 years ago.

s: Madhava of Sangamagrama was a mathematician and astronomer who founded the Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics at Irinjalakuda in Kerala.
k: Madhava was a mathematician from Kerala who lived about 600 years ago. He started a famous school of mathematics.

s: Kabir, who flourished in the 15th century, was a devotional mystic poet and saint, born in Varanasi and known for being critical of organised religions. His verses are found in the Sikh scripture. Historians differ on his dates, some favouring 1398–1448 and others 1440–1518.
k: Kabir was a poet and saint from Varanasi who lived in the 1400s. He said that people argued too much about religion. His poems are still sung.

s: Narsinh Mehta was a 15th-century poet-saint of Gujarat, honoured as the first poet, or Adi Kavi, of the Gujarati language.
k: Narsinh Mehta was a poet and saint of Gujarat. He is honoured as the first poet of the Gujarati language.

s: Nilakantha Somayaji was a mathematician and astronomer of the Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics.
k: Nilakantha was a mathematician and astronomer of the Kerala school.

s: Srimanta Sankardev was a 15th–16th-century Assamese polymath: a saint-scholar, poet, playwright, dancer, actor, musician, artist and social-religious reformer.
k: Sankardev of Assam was a saint, poet, playwright, dancer and musician all at once. The dance called Sattriya began with his plays.

s: Ravidas, or Raidas, was a mystic poet-saint of the Bhakti movement during the 15th to 16th century CE, venerated as a guru in several regions of northern India.
k: Ravidas was a poet and saint who lived about 500 years ago. Many people in northern India still honour him as their guru.

s: Purandara Dasa was a composer, singer and philosopher from present-day Karnataka.
k: Purandara Dasa was a singer and composer from Karnataka who lived about 500 years ago.

s: Krishnadevaraya was emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529 and the third ruler of the Tuluva dynasty. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest rulers of India.
k: Krishnadevaraya was the most famous emperor of Vijayanagara. He ruled from 1509 to 1529.

s: Babur, born at Andijan in the Fergana Valley, was the founder of the Mughal Empire. He was descended from Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's.
k: Babur was born in Central Asia. He invaded India and founded the Mughal Empire in 1526.

s: Sher Shah Suri was the first Sur emperor, ruling as Sultan of Hindustan from 1540 until his death in 1545.
k: Sher Shah Suri took northern India from the Mughals and ruled it from 1540 to 1545.

s: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, born Vishvambhara Mishra, was a Hindu saint from Bengal and the founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism.
k: Chaitanya was a Hindu saint from Bengal who founded a new religious tradition.

s: Tulsidas was a Hindu saint and poet renowned for his devotion to Rama. He composed the Ramcharitmanas, an epic poem in the Awadhi language.
k: Tulsidas was a poet who retold the story of Rama in the Awadhi language.

s: Akbar, known as Akbar the Great, was the third Mughal emperor, reigning from 1556 to 1605. He succeeded his father Humayun under a regent, Bairam Khan.
k: Akbar became Mughal emperor in 1556, when he was still a boy, and ruled until 1605. He is known as Akbar the Great.

s: Malik Ambar was a military leader and statesman who served as Peshwa of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate and was its de facto ruler from 1600 until his death in 1626.
k: Malik Ambar was a general who became the real ruler of the kingdom of Ahmadnagar in the Deccan from 1600 to 1626.

s: Meera, better known as Mirabai, was a 16th-century Hindu mystic poet and devotee of Krishna. She was born into a Rathore Rajput royal family in today's Rajasthan and spent her childhood in Merta.
k: Mirabai was a princess of Rajasthan who lived about 500 years ago. She gave her life to singing songs of love for the god Krishna.

s: Surdas was a 16th-century blind Hindu devotional poet and singer, known for works written in praise of Krishna.
k: Surdas was a blind poet and singer who lived about 500 years ago. He sang about the god Krishna.

s: Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak was a writer, historian and politician who served as grand vizier of the Mughal Empire. He wrote the Akbarnama and the Ain-i-Akbari.
k: Abul Fazl was the emperor Akbar's chief minister and historian. He wrote the story of Akbar's reign.

s: Nur Jahan, born Mehr-un-Nissa, was the chief consort of the Mughal emperor Jahangir. More decisive and proactive than her husband, she is considered by some historians to have been the real power behind the throne.
k: Nur Jahan was the wife of the Mughal emperor Jahangir. She was so clever and bold that some historians say she was the real ruler.

s: Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal emperor, from 1628 until he was deposed in 1658. His reign marked the zenith of Mughal architecture.
k: Shah Jahan was the Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal. He ruled from 1628 to 1658.

s: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son and heir-apparent of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
k: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of the emperor Shah Jahan and was meant to be the next emperor.

s: Aurangzeb, also called Alamgir I, was the sixth Mughal emperor, reigning from 1658 until his death in 1707. Under him the empire reached its greatest extent.
k: Aurangzeb was the sixth Mughal emperor. He ruled for almost fifty years, and the empire was at its biggest in his time.

s: Lachit Borphukan was an army general who commanded the Ahom army to victory in the naval Battle of Saraighat, stopping a Mughal invasion.
k: Lachit Borphukan was the general of the Ahom kingdom of Assam. In 1671 he beat the Mughal navy on the Brahmaputra river.

s: Shivaji was an Indian ruler of the Bhonsle dynasty, born at the hill-fort of Shivneri. He inherited a fief from his father, who served the Sultanate of Bijapur, and founded the Maratha kingdom, being crowned in 1674.
k: Shivaji was born in a hill fort in 1630. He built up his own kingdom and was crowned king of the Marathas in 1674.

s: Tukaram, also known as Tukoba, was a Hindu Marathi saint of the Varkari tradition who lived in the 17th century.
k: Tukaram was a saint of Maharashtra who lived about 400 years ago. He sang his poems in Marathi.

s: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last human Sikh Guru: a warrior, poet and philosopher. In 1675, at the age of nine, he was formally made the leader of the Sikhs. In 1699 he founded the Khalsa.
k: Guru Gobind Singh became the leader of the Sikhs when he was only nine. He was a warrior and a poet, and he founded the Khalsa in 1699.

s: Sawai Jai Singh II was the ruler of the Kingdom of Amber who founded the fortified city of Jaipur and made it his capital. He built the Jantar Mantar, a collection of astronomical instruments.
k: Sawai Jai Singh was a king who founded the city of Jaipur and built giant instruments there to study the sky.

s: Bajirao I was the seventh Peshwa of the Maratha Empire, the son of Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath. He began his military career at a young age.
k: Bajirao was the chief minister and general of the Marathas. He began fighting when he was very young.

s: Ahilyabai Holkar was the Holkar queen of the Malwa kingdom and later ruling queen of Indore within the Maratha Empire. She is remembered for her contributions to Hindu cultural institutions.
k: Ahilyabai Holkar was a queen who ruled Indore, in the Maratha Empire, about 250 years ago. She is remembered for the temples she helped to build and repair.

s: Tilka Majhi, according to popular accounts, was a tribal leader who led a rebellion against British colonial rule from 1771 until his capture and execution in 1785.
k: Stories tell that Tilka Majhi, a tribal leader, fought the British from 1771 until they caught and killed him in 1785.

s: Tipu Sultan, known as Sher-e-Mysore, was Sultan of Mysore from 1782 until his death in 1799. He was a pioneer of rocket artillery.
k: Tipu Sultan ruled Mysore from 1782 to 1799. His army used rockets in battle, which was new.

s: Dean Mahomed was a traveller, soldier, surgeon and entrepreneur from British India, and one of the most notable early non-European immigrants to the Western world.
k: Dean Mahomed, born in 1759, was an Indian soldier and traveller who settled in Europe and started businesses there. He was one of the first Indians to make a life in the West.

s: Tyagaraja was a composer of Carnatic music, a form of Indian classical music. He lived through the reigns of four kings of the Thanjavur Maratha line but served none of them.
k: Tyagaraja was one of the greatest composers of south Indian classical music. Kings ruled where he lived, but he would not work for any of them.

s: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a social reformer and writer, one of the founders in 1828 of the Brahmo Sabha, the precursor of the Brahmo Samaj.
k: Ram Mohan Roy was a thinker from Bengal who wanted to change harmful old customs. In 1828 he helped to start a movement to reform religion.

s: Bahadur Shah II, known by his poetic title Zafar, was the twentieth and last Mughal emperor and an Urdu poet. He was emperor in title only.
k: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor. He had almost no power, and he wrote poetry in Urdu.

s: Mirza Asadullah Beg Khan, known as Mirza Ghalib, was a poet and letter writer who wrote during the final years of the Mughal Empire and the rise of British rule.
k: Mirza Ghalib was a great poet who lived in the last days of the Mughal emperors.

s: Ranjit Singh was the founder and first maharaja of the Sikh Empire, ruling from 1801 until his death in 1839. He fought his first battle alongside his father at the age of ten.
k: Maharaja Ranjit Singh founded the Sikh Empire. He fought his first battle when he was ten years old.

s: Rashsundari Devi, born in eastern Bengal, is identified as the author of the first full autobiography in modern Bengali literature. She was the first Indian woman to write an autobiography.
k: Rashsundari Devi was a Bengali woman who wrote the story of her own life. No Indian woman had written such a book before.

s: Radhanath Sikdar was a mathematician and social reformer, best known as the first person to calculate the height of Mount Everest, in 1852.
k: In 1852 a mathematician named Radhanath Sikdar worked out the height of Mount Everest. He was the first person to do it.

s: Tantia Tope was an Indian general in the Indian Rebellion of 1857 against the British East India Company.
k: Tatya Tope was a general who fought the British in the great rebellion of 1857.

s: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was a Muslim reformer, philosopher and educationist of nineteenth-century British India. In 1875 he established the college that became Aligarh Muslim University.
k: Syed Ahmad Khan was a Muslim reformer and educator. In 1875 he founded a college at Aligarh.

s: Begum Hazrat Mahal, the Begum of Awadh, was the second wife of the Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah, and regent of Awadh in 1857–1858. She is known for her leading role in the rebellion.
k: Begum Hazrat Mahal ruled Awadh during the rebellion of 1857 and led the fight against the British there.

s: Ishwar Chandra Bandyopadhyay, known as Vidyasagar, was an educator and social reformer of the 19th century, and the most prominent campaigner for the remarriage of Hindu widows.
k: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a teacher and reformer. He campaigned for the right of Hindu widows to marry again.

s: Dayanand Saraswati, born Mool Shankar Tiwari, was a Hindu philosopher and social leader and the founder of the Arya Samaj, a reform movement of Hinduism.
k: Dayanand Saraswati was a Hindu teacher who founded a reform movement called the Arya Samaj.

s: Jyotirao Phule, also known as Jyotiba Phule, was a social activist, businessman, anti-caste social reformer and writer from Maharashtra. With his followers he formed the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers) to win equal rights for people from lower castes.
k: Jyotirao Phule fought against the unfair treatment of people by caste. With his wife Savitribai he opened schools for girls.

s: Nain Singh Rawat, from the Johar Valley in Kumaon, was one of the first Indian explorers employed by the British to explore the Himalayas and Central Asia.
k: Nain Singh Rawat was an explorer from the Himalaya who explored the mountains and Central Asia for the British.

s: Savitribai Phule was an educator, social reformer and poet, widely regarded as the first Indian female teacher. In 1848, with her husband Jyotirao Phule and Sagunabai Kshirsagar, she established a school for girls in Pune.
k: Savitribai Phule is remembered as India's first woman teacher. In 1848 she and her husband opened a school for girls in Pune.

s: Lakshmibai, born Manikarnika Tambe into a Marathi family in Varanasi, was married young to the raja of Jhansi. She was one of the leading figures of the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and died on 18 June 1858. Her year of birth is uncertain.
k: Lakshmibai, the Rani of Jhansi, was a queen who became one of the leaders of the great rebellion of 1857. She died in 1858.

s: Ramakrishna, born Ramakrishna Chattopadhyay at Kamarpukur in Bengal, was a Hindu mystic and a devotee of the goddess Kali.
k: Ramakrishna was a holy man of Bengal who was devoted to the goddess Kali.

s: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was a Bengali novelist, poet, essayist and journalist. He wrote the poem "Vande Mataram", first published in 1882.
k: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee was a Bengali novelist. He wrote the poem "Vande Mataram", which became India's national song.

s: Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata, born into a Parsi family of priests in Navsari, was an industrialist and philanthropist who founded the Tata Group, India's largest conglomerate.
k: Jamsetji Tata was born in Navsari. He founded the Tata group of companies, the biggest in India.

s: C. Iyothee Thassa Pandithar was an anti-caste activist and a practitioner of Siddha medicine. He converted to Buddhism and called on the Paraiyars to do the same.
k: Iyothee Thass was a doctor of traditional Tamil medicine who fought against caste. He became a Buddhist and asked his community to do so too.

s: Annie Besant was an English socialist, theosophist, educationist and activist involved in women's rights, Home Rule and Indian nationalism. In 1917 she was among the founders of the Women's Indian Association at Adyar.
k: Annie Besant was an Englishwoman who worked for India's self-rule and for women's rights.

s: Raja Ravi Varma was a painter whose works are among the best examples of the fusion of European academic art with a purely Indian sensibility and iconography.
k: Raja Ravi Varma was a painter who mixed European ways of painting with Indian stories and gods.

s: Fatima Sheikh was a 19th-century educator and social reformer, a colleague of the reformers Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule.
k: Fatima Sheikh was a teacher who worked with Savitribai Phule in the 1800s.

s: Tarabai Shinde was a feminist activist who protested against patriarchy and caste in 19th-century India. She is known for her published work Stri Purush Tulana.
k: Tarabai Shinde protested against the unfair treatment of women in the 1800s. She is known for a book she published.

s: Tirot Sing, also known as U Tirot Sing Syiem, was one of the chiefs of the Khasi people in the early 19th century.
k: Tirot Sing was a chief of the Khasi people in the early 1800s.

s: Sido Murmu and Kanhu Murmu were brothers who led the Santhal Rebellion of 1855 in present-day Jharkhand and parts of Bengal.
k: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu were two Santal brothers who led their people in a great uprising in 1855.

s: Tarulatta Datta, known as Toru Dutt, was a Bengali poet and translator who wrote in English and French. She died at 21.
k: Toru Dutt was a young Bengali poet who wrote in English and French. She died when she was only 21.

s: Sree Narayana Guru was a philosopher, spiritual leader and social reformer who led a reform movement against injustice in the caste-ridden society of Kerala.
k: Narayana Guru was a holy man of Kerala who taught that all people are equal, whatever their caste.

s: Mangal Pandey, who died on 8 April 1857, was a soldier who played a key role in the events that led to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
k: Mangal Pandey was an Indian soldier who played a key part in the events that led to the great rebellion of 1857.

s: Pandita Ramabai Sarasvati was a social reformer and Christian missionary, the first woman to be awarded the titles of Pandita, as a Sanskrit scholar, and Sarasvati.
k: Pandita Ramabai was such a fine scholar of Sanskrit that she was given the title Pandita, the first woman to have it. She worked to help women and girls.

s: Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose, born at Mymensingh in the Bengal Presidency, was a polymath with interests in biology and physics, a pioneer in the investigation of radio microwave optics, and a writer of science fiction.
k: Jagadish Chandra Bose was a scientist from Bengal who studied radio waves and plants. He also wrote science fiction stories.

s: Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali polymath: poet, author, playwright, composer, philosopher, social reformer and painter. He received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913.
k: Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet, songwriter, painter and teacher. In 1913 he won the Nobel Prize for his poems.

s: Kadambini Bose Ganguly was, with Anandibai Joshi, the first Indian woman doctor of western medicine. Both took their degrees in 1886. She was India's first practising woman doctor.
k: Kadambini Ganguly became a doctor in 1886. She was the first Indian woman to work as a doctor.

s: Sir Prafulla Chandra Ray was a chemist, educationist, historian, industrialist and philanthropist from Bengal.
k: Prafulla Chandra Ray was a chemist from Bengal who was also a teacher and a founder of industry.

s: Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya was a civil engineer, administrator and statesman who served as the 19th Dewan of Mysore.
k: M. Visvesvaraya was a great engineer who became chief minister of the kingdom of Mysore.

s: Bhikhaiji Rustom Cama, known as Madam Cama, was one of the prominent figures of the Indian independence movement. She unfurled one of the earliest versions of the flag of India.
k: Madam Cama worked for India's freedom. She raised one of the first flags of a free India.

s: Swami Vivekananda, born Narendranath Datta, was a Hindu monk, philosopher and religious teacher, the chief disciple of the mystic Ramakrishna. He founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897.
k: Swami Vivekananda was a monk and the best-known pupil of Ramakrishna. In 1897 he founded the Ramakrishna Mission.

s: Ayyankali was a social reformer, educator, lawmaker and revolutionary leader who worked for the advancement of oppressed people in the princely state of Travancore.
k: Ayyankali was a leader in Kerala who worked for the advancement of oppressed people.

s: Rukhmabai was a physician and feminist, best known as one of the first practising women doctors in colonial India, and for her part in a landmark legal case.
k: Rukhmabai was one of the first Indian women to work as a doctor.

s: Lala Lajpat Rai was a nationalist and author, popularly known as Punjab Kesari, and one of the three members of the Lal Bal Pal trio.
k: Lala Lajpat Rai was a freedom fighter from the Punjab. People called him Punjab Kesari.

s: Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi was the first certified Indian woman doctor of western medicine. She graduated with a two-year degree in western medicine in the United States, and died in 1887 aged 21.
k: Anandibai Joshi went to the United States to study and became a doctor. She died in 1887, when she was only 21.

s: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a political leader and social reformer during the Indian independence movement, and the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.
k: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a leader of the freedom movement. Mahatma Gandhi called him his teacher in politics.

s: Cornelia Sorabji was a lawyer, social reformer and writer. She was the first female graduate of Bombay University and the first woman to study law at Oxford University.
k: Cornelia Sorabji was the first woman to graduate from Bombay University and the first woman to study law at Oxford.

s: Kasturba Gandhi was a political activist involved in the Indian independence movement. She was married to Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.
k: Kasturba Gandhi was Mahatma Gandhi's wife and took part in the freedom struggle herself.

s: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was a lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist and political ethicist who employed nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule. He was assassinated on 30 January 1948.
k: Mahatma Gandhi led India's struggle for freedom without using violence. He was killed in 1948, a few months after India became free.

s: Matangini Hazra was a revolutionary of the independence movement. On 29 September 1942, aged 71, she was leading a group of volunteers towards the Tamluk police station when the police shot her dead.
k: Matangini Hazra was 71 years old when she led a march for freedom at Tamluk in 1942. The police shot her.

s: Sri Aurobindo was a philosopher, yogi and nationalist, noted for his part in the movement for India's independence. In 1926 he founded an ashram in Pondicherry.
k: Sri Aurobindo first worked for India's freedom and then became a philosopher and teacher of yoga in Pondicherry.

s: Vallabhbhai Patel, known as Sardar Patel, born in Nadiad in Gujarat, was an independence activist, lawyer and statesman who served as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India.
k: Sardar Patel was a freedom fighter from Gujarat. He became independent India's first Deputy Prime Minister.

s: Birsa Munda, of the Munda tribe, was a tribal independence activist and folk hero who led a tribal religious movement. He died at 24.
k: Birsa Munda was a young leader of the Munda people who stood up to British rule. He died when he was only 24, and is remembered as a hero.

s: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, born in Karachi and trained as a barrister in London, was the founder of Pakistan. He led the All-India Muslim League from 1913 until independence.
k: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was a lawyer born in Karachi. He led the Muslim League and founded the country of Pakistan.

s: Sir Muhammad Iqbal was an Islamic philosopher and poet whose poetry in Urdu is considered among the greatest of the 20th century.
k: Muhammad Iqbal was a philosopher and one of the greatest Urdu poets of the 1900s.

s: Chakravarti Rajagopalachari, known as Rajaji, born in a village of today's Tamil Nadu, was a statesman, writer, lawyer and independence activist.
k: Rajaji was a freedom fighter, writer and statesman from Tamil Nadu.

s: Sarojini Naidu, born into a Bengali family in Hyderabad, was a political activist and poet. She was appointed Congress president in 1925 and became the first Governor of the United Provinces after independence.
k: Sarojini Naidu was a poet and a leader of the freedom movement. In 1925 she became president of the Congress.

s: Erode Venkatappa Ramasamy, known as Periyar, was a social activist and politician, the organiser of the Self-Respect Movement and the Dravidar Kazhagam.
k: Periyar led a movement in the Tamil country that told people of every caste to respect themselves and demand equal treatment.

s: Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, better known by his pen name Premchand, was a writer famous for his modern Hindustani literature.
k: Premchand was one of the most famous writers of stories and novels in Hindustani.

s: Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain, known as Begum Rokeya, was a Bengali feminist thinker, writer, educator and political activist. In 1916 she founded the Muslim Women's Association, which fought for women's education and employment.
k: Begum Rokeya was a Bengali writer and teacher who fought for the right of women and girls to study and to work.

s: Subramania Bharati, born at Ettayapuram in 1882, was a writer, poet, journalist, independence activist and social reformer.
k: Subramania Bharati was a great Tamil poet who wrote about freedom.

s: Rajendra Prasad was a politician, lawyer, journalist and scholar who served as the first President of India, from 1950 to 1962.
k: Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India, from 1950 to 1962.

s: Jamini Roy was a painter, one of the most famous pupils of Abanindranath Tagore. He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 1954.
k: Jamini Roy was a famous painter.

s: Srinivasa Ramanujan was a mathematician who worked during the early 20th century and made substantial contributions to mathematical analysis and number theory. He died at 32.
k: Srinivasa Ramanujan was a genius with numbers. He made amazing discoveries in mathematics before he died at the age of 32.

s: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was an academic, philosopher and statesman who served as Vice President of India from 1952 to 1962 and as President from 1962.
k: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was a philosopher and teacher who became President of India in 1962.

s: Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman, born in today's Tamil Nadu, was a physicist known for his work on the scattering of light. The effect he discovered is called Raman scattering.
k: C. V. Raman was a physicist who discovered something new about how light scatters. The effect is named after him.

s: Abul Kalam Ghulam Muhiyuddin, better known as Maulana Azad, was a writer and an activist of the Indian independence movement.
k: Maulana Azad was a writer and a leader of the freedom movement.

s: Jawaharlal Nehru was a lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist and statesman, a central figure in India in the middle of the 20th century and its first Prime Minister.
k: Jawaharlal Nehru was a leader of the freedom struggle and became the first Prime Minister of independent India.

s: Khudiram Bose was a nationalist from the Bengal Presidency who opposed British rule. For his part in the Muzaffarpur Conspiracy Case, an attempt to kill a British judge, he was sentenced to death. He died on 11 August 1908, aged 18.
k: Khudiram Bose was a teenager from Bengal who fought British rule. He was sentenced to death and died in 1908, when he was 18.

s: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as Bacha Khan, was an independence activist from the North-West Frontier Province and the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgar movement.
k: Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a freedom fighter from the north-west frontier.

s: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a jurist, economist, social reformer and politician who chaired the committee that drafted the Constitution of India. In 1956 he became a Buddhist, with nearly half a million followers.
k: Dr Ambedkar was a jurist and reformer who led the writing of India's Constitution and fought against caste discrimination. Late in life he became a Buddhist.

s: Birbal Sahni was a paleobotanist who studied the fossils of the Indian subcontinent. He also took an interest in geology and archaeology.
k: Birbal Sahni was a scientist who studied fossil plants found in India.

s: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was a scientist and statistician, best remembered for the Mahalanobis distance, a statistical measure.
k: P. C. Mahalanobis was a scientist of numbers and statistics. A measure used in statistics is named after him.

s: Meghnad Saha was an astrophysicist and politician who helped devise the theory of thermal ionisation. His Saha ionisation equation is used by astronomers.
k: Meghnad Saha was a scientist who worked out an equation that helps astronomers understand the stars.

s: Satyendra Nath Bose was a theoretical physicist and mathematician, best known for his work on quantum mechanics in the early 1920s.
k: Satyendra Nath Bose was a physicist who did famous work on the tiniest particles in the 1920s.

s: Yellapragada Subbarao was an Indian American biochemist who discovered the function of adenosine triphosphate as an energy source in the cell and developed the drug methotrexate.
k: Yellapragada Subbarao was a scientist who discovered how living cells store their energy, and helped make important medicines.

s: Vinayak Narahar Bhave, known as Vinoba Bhave, was a philosopher and an advocate of nonviolence and human rights. In 1951 he began the Bhoodan movement for voluntary land reform.
k: Vinoba Bhave was a follower of Gandhi. In 1951 he started a movement asking landowners to give land to the poor.

s: Salim Ali was an ornithologist and naturalist, sometimes called the "Birdman of India". He was the first Indian to conduct systematic bird surveys across the country.
k: Salim Ali loved birds. He was the first Indian to count and study the birds of the whole country, and people called him the Birdman of India.

s: Subhas Chandra Bose, born into a large Bengali family in Orissa, was an anti-colonial nationalist whose defiance of British authority made him a hero to many Indians. His wartime alliances with Nazi Germany and Japan left a troubled legacy. He led the Indian National Army.
k: Subhas Chandra Bose wanted to free India by force. During the Second World War he led an army that fought alongside Japan against the British. Many Indians see him as a hero, but his choice of allies is still argued about.

s: Hansa Jivraj Mehta was a reformist, social activist, educator, independence activist, feminist and writer.
k: Hansa Mehta was a writer and teacher who worked for India's freedom and for the rights of women.

s: Alluri Sitarama Raju, born into a Telugu family in the Madras Presidency, was a revolutionary who waged an armed rebellion and guerrilla campaigns against British colonial rule. He led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922.
k: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the tribal people of the Godavari hills in a rebellion against the British in 1922.

s: Edavalath Kakkat Janaki Ammal was a botanist who worked on plant breeding, cytogenetics and phytogeography. Her most notable work involved studies of sugarcane.
k: Janaki Ammal was a botanist, a scientist of plants. She is best known for her work on sugarcane.

s: Kazi Nazrul Islam, born at Churulia in the Bengal Presidency, was a Bengali poet, short story writer, journalist, lyricist and musician. He was later honoured as the national poet of Bangladesh.
k: Kazi Nazrul Islam was a Bengali poet and songwriter. He is the national poet of Bangladesh.

s: Udham Singh was a revolutionary of the Ghadar Party, best known for assassinating Michael O'Dwyer, the former lieutenant governor of the Punjab.
k: Udham Singh was a revolutionary from the Punjab who killed a former British governor.

s: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was a freedom fighter, diplomat and politician. She served as the 8th President of the United Nations General Assembly, from 1953 to 1954.
k: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was a freedom fighter who later became President of the United Nations General Assembly.

s: Komaram Bheem was a revolutionary leader from the Gond tribes in Hyderabad State.
k: Komaram Bheem was a leader of the Gond people who fought for their rights in Hyderabad State.

s: Jayaprakash Narayan, known as JP and Lok Nayak, was a politician, theorist and independence activist.
k: Jayaprakash Narayan, known as JP, was a freedom fighter and political leader.

s: Jaipal Singh Munda was a politician, writer and sportsman. He captained the Indian hockey team to a gold medal at the 1928 Olympics, sat in the Constituent Assembly, and campaigned for the causes of Adivasis.
k: Jaipal Singh Munda was captain of the Indian hockey team that won Olympic gold in 1928. Later he became a leader who spoke up for India's Adivasi peoples.

s: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay was a social reformer who worked for the promotion of Indian handicrafts, handlooms and theatre in independent India.
k: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay worked to save India's handicrafts, hand-weaving and theatre.

s: Kumaraswami Kamaraj, popularly known as Kamarajar, was an independence activist, politician, social reformer and statesman.
k: K. Kamaraj was a freedom fighter, politician and social reformer.

s: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a theosophist, a dancer and choreographer of the classical dance form Bharatanatyam, and an activist for animal welfare.
k: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a dancer and choreographer of the classical dance Bharatanatyam. She also worked for the welfare of animals.

s: Lal Bahadur Shastri, born at Mughalsarai on 2 October 1904, was a politician and statesman who served as Prime Minister of India from 1964 to 1966.
k: Lal Bahadur Shastri was Prime Minister of India from 1964 to 1966.

s: Major Dhyan Chand was a field hockey player, widely regarded as the greatest in the history of the game, known for his extraordinary ball control.
k: Dhyan Chand is thought by many to be the greatest hockey player who ever lived.

s: Chandra Shekhar Sitaram Tiwari, known as Chandra Shekhar Azad, was a revolutionary who reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association under a new name.
k: Chandra Shekhar Azad was a young revolutionary who fought British rule.

s: Rasipuram Krishnaswami Narayanaswami, better known as R. K. Narayan, was a writer and novelist known for his work set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi.
k: R. K. Narayan wrote stories about a made-up town in southern India called Malgudi.

s: Mahadevi Varma was a Hindi-language poet, essayist and short-story writer, regarded as one of the four major pillars of the Chhayavaad movement in Hindi literature.
k: Mahadevi Varma was a famous poet and writer in the Hindi language.

s: Bhagat Singh was an anti-colonial revolutionary. He was convicted of murder and hanged in March 1931, aged 23.
k: Bhagat Singh was a young revolutionary who fought British rule. He was hanged in 1931, when he was 23.

s: Vaikom Muhammad Basheer, popularly called the Beypore Sultan, was a writer of Malayalam literature, a humanist and a freedom fighter.
k: Basheer was a much-loved writer in the Malayalam language. He also took part in the freedom struggle.

s: Jagjivan Ram, popularly known as Babuji, was an independence activist and politician who served as a minister with various portfolios for over 30 years.
k: Jagjivan Ram was a freedom fighter who served as a government minister for more than thirty years.

s: Sucheta Kripalani was a politician and independence activist. She was India's first female Chief Minister, as head of the Uttar Pradesh government.
k: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman to become Chief Minister of an Indian state.

s: Durgabai Deshmukh was a freedom fighter, lawyer, social worker and politician, a member of the Constituent Assembly of India and of the Planning Commission.
k: Durgabai Deshmukh was a freedom fighter and lawyer who helped to write India's Constitution.

s: Aruna Asaf Ali was an educator, political activist and publisher, widely remembered for hoisting the Indian national flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay during the Quit India Movement of 1942.
k: In 1942 Aruna Asaf Ali raised the Indian flag at a great meeting ground in Bombay during the Quit India protests.

s: Homi Jehangir Bhabha was a nuclear physicist widely credited as the "father of the Indian nuclear programme". In January 1954 he founded the research establishment at Trombay that now bears his name.
k: Homi Bhabha was a physicist who started India's atomic research. People call him the father of India's nuclear programme.

s: Mother Teresa, born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu in Skopje, was an Albanian-Indian Catholic nun and the founder of the Missionaries of Charity. She is known as Saint Mother Teresa of Calcutta.
k: Mother Teresa was a Catholic nun born far away in Skopje. She came to Calcutta and founded a group of sisters to care for people in need.

s: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was an Indian-American astrophysicist who shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for his theoretical studies of the physical processes in stars.
k: Chandrasekhar was a scientist who worked out how stars live and die. He won the Nobel Prize in 1983.

s: Faiz Ahmad Faiz, born in the Punjab and educated in Lahore, was a Pakistani poet and author, one of the best-known Urdu writers of his time.
k: Faiz Ahmad Faiz was one of the best-known Urdu poets of the 1900s.

s: Pritilata Waddedar was a Bengali revolutionary nationalist from Chittagong who was influential in the Indian independence movement. She died at 21.
k: Pritilata Waddedar was a young woman from Chittagong who joined the revolutionaries fighting British rule. She died when she was 21.

s: Kamala Sohonie was a biochemist who in 1939 became the first Indian woman to receive a PhD in a scientific discipline.
k: In 1939 Kamala Sohonie became the first Indian woman to earn a doctorate in science.

s: Ismat Chughtai was an Urdu novelist, short story writer and filmmaker. From the 1930s she wrote extensively on themes that included women's lives.
k: Ismat Chughtai was a bold writer of stories in Urdu, many of them about the lives of women.

s: Saadat Hasan Manto was a writer, playwright and novelist from Punjab, regarded as the greatest short-story author in Urdu literature.
k: Manto is thought by many to be the greatest writer of short stories in Urdu.

s: Dakshayani Velayudhan was a politician and a leader of the oppressed classes, belonging to the Pulayar community.
k: Dakshayani Velayudhan was a leader of people who had been treated as low caste. She came from the Pulayar community.

s: Amrita Sher-Gil was a Hungarian–Indian painter who has been called one of the greatest avant-garde women artists of the early 20th century. She died at 28.
k: Amrita Sher-Gil was a Hungarian–Indian painter. She painted famous pictures before she died at only 28.

s: Bibha Chowdhuri was a particle physicist known for her investigations of cosmic rays, on which she worked with D. M. Bose.
k: Bibha Chowdhuri was a physicist who studied cosmic rays.

s: Dhundiraj Govind Phalke, known as Dadasaheb Phalke, was a producer, director and screenwriter, widely regarded as "the Father of Indian cinema". His film Raja Harishchandra premiered in Bombay in 1913.
k: Dadasaheb Phalke made India's first full-length film in 1913. People call him the father of Indian cinema.

s: Tenzing Norgay, born Namgyal Wangdi, was a Nepalese-Indian Sherpa mountaineer. On 29 May 1953 he and Edmund Hillary became the first people known to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
k: On 29 May 1953 Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary became the first people to stand on top of Mount Everest.

s: Akhtari Bai Faizabadi, known as Begum Akhtar, was a singer and actress. Called Mallika-e-Ghazal, she is regarded as one of the greatest singers of that form.
k: Begum Akhtar was a singer famous for her ghazals, a kind of song made from poetry.

s: Lakshmi Sahgal was a revolutionary of the independence movement, an officer of the Indian National Army and a minister in the Azad Hind government. In 1998 she was awarded the Padma Vibhushan.
k: Lakshmi Sahgal was an officer in the Indian National Army, which fought for India's freedom.

s: Murlidhar Devidas Amte, known as Baba Amte, was a social worker and activist known particularly for his work for the rehabilitation and empowerment of people suffering from leprosy.
k: Baba Amte spent his life caring for people who had leprosy and helping them to live with dignity.

s: Gaidinliu Pamei, known as Rani Gaidinliu, was a Naga spiritual and political leader who led a revolt against British rule. She joined the movement at 13, was arrested in 1932 at 16, and was sentenced to life imprisonment.
k: Gaidinliu was a Naga girl who joined a movement against British rule when she was 13. At 16 she was arrested and sent to prison for life.

s: Maqbool Fida Husain was a painter and film director who painted narrative paintings in a modified Cubist style. He was one of the founding members of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group.
k: M. F. Husain was one of India's most famous modern painters.

s: Ustad Bismillah Khan, born Qamaruddin Khan, was a musician credited with popularising the shehnai, a reeded woodwind instrument.
k: Bismillah Khan played the shehnai, a wind instrument, so beautifully that he made it famous.

s: Madurai Shanmukhavadivu Subbulakshmi was a Carnatic singer and the first musician ever to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour.
k: M. S. Subbulakshmi was a great singer of south Indian classical music. She was the first musician to win India's highest honour.

s: Asima Chatterjee was an organic chemist noted for her work in organic chemistry and phytomedicine, the study of medicines from plants.
k: Asima Chatterjee was a chemist who studied medicines that come from plants.

s: Indira Gandhi served as Prime Minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984. She was India's first and only female prime minister.
k: Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister of India for many years. She is the only woman to have held the job. She was killed in 1984.

s: Tanjore Balasaraswati was a dancer celebrated for her rendering of Bharatanatyam, a classical dance style of South India.
k: Balasaraswati was one of the greatest dancers of Bharatanatyam.

s: Anna Mani was a physicist and meteorologist who retired as deputy director general of the Indian Meteorological Department.
k: Anna Mani was a scientist of the weather who rose to be one of the heads of India's weather service.

s: Vikram Ambalal Sarabhai was a physicist and astronomer who initiated space research and helped to develop nuclear power in India. He is often regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.
k: Vikram Sarabhai was the scientist who started India's space programme.

s: Amrita Pritam was a novelist, essayist and poet who wrote in Punjabi and Hindi, a prominent figure in Punjabi literature.
k: Amrita Pritam was a famous poet and novelist who wrote in Punjabi.

s: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, born at Tungipara, was a Bangladeshi politician and statesman, the founding president of Bangladesh.
k: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman led the people of East Pakistan to freedom and became the first president of Bangladesh.

s: Kocheril Raman Narayanan, born in a village of the princely state of Travancore, was a diplomat, academic and statesman who served as President of India from 1997 to 2002.
k: K. R. Narayanan was born in a village in Kerala and became President of India in 1997.

s: Satyajit Ray, born in Calcutta, was a film director, screenwriter, author, illustrator and composer. His first film as director was Pather Panchali, in 1955.
k: Satyajit Ray was a film-maker from Calcutta. His films, beginning with Pather Panchali in 1955, are famous all over the world.

s: Verghese Kurien was a dairy engineer and social entrepreneur who led the initiatives that greatly increased milk production in India.
k: Verghese Kurien helped India's dairy farmers work together and produce far more milk.

s: Har Gobind Khorana, born at Raipur in the Punjab, was an Indian-American biochemist who shared the 1968 Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine.
k: Har Gobind Khorana was born in a village in the Punjab. He became a scientist in America and won the Nobel Prize in 1968.

s: Rajeshwari Chatterjee was a scientist and academic, the first woman engineer from Karnataka.
k: Rajeshwari Chatterjee was the first woman from Karnataka to become an engineer.

s: Gaura Devi was a grassroots activist and rural women's community leader who played an important role in the Chipko movement.
k: Gaura Devi was a village woman who led other women in protecting their forest in the Chipko movement.

s: Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan was a geneticist and plant breeder, administrator and humanitarian who was a global leader of the green revolution.
k: M. S. Swaminathan was a plant scientist who helped India's farmers grow much more food.

s: Mahasweta Devi was a Bengali-language writer and activist. Her notable works include Hajar Churashir Maa, Rudali and Aranyer Adhikar.
k: Mahasweta Devi was a Bengali writer and activist.

s: Sunderlal Bahuguna was an environmentalist and a leader of the Chipko movement, whose idea was suggested by him and his wife, Vimla Bahuguna.
k: Sunderlal Bahuguna was a leader of the Chipko movement to save the forests.

s: Lata Mangeshkar was a playback singer and occasional composer, considered one of the greatest and most influential singers of the Indian subcontinent.
k: Lata Mangeshkar sang the songs for a great many Indian films. She is thought of as one of the greatest singers of the Indian subcontinent.

s: Milkha Singh, known as "The Flying Sikh", was a track and field sprinter who was introduced to the sport while serving in the Indian Army.
k: Milkha Singh was a runner so fast that people called him the Flying Sikh. He began running when he was a soldier.

s: Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam was an aerospace engineer and science administrator who served as President of India from 2002 to 2007.
k: Abdul Kalam was a rocket engineer who became President of India in 2002.

s: Elattuvalapil Sreedharan is an engineer from Kerala known for leading the construction of numerous large projects.
k: E. Sreedharan is an engineer from Kerala who led the building of many big projects.

s: Manmohan Singh, born at Gah in what is today Pakistan, was an economist and statesman who served as Prime Minister of India from 2004 to 2014. His family migrated to India at the partition of 1947.
k: Manmohan Singh was born in a village that is now in Pakistan. His family moved to India in 1947. He became an economist and then Prime Minister.

s: Ela Ramesh Bhatt was a cooperative organiser, activist and Gandhian who founded the Self-Employed Women's Association of India in 1972.
k: Ela Bhatt started a union for poor working women in 1972.

s: Amartya Kumar Sen is an economist and philosopher who has taught and worked in England and the United States since 1972. In 1998 he received the Nobel Prize.
k: Amartya Sen is an economist and thinker who won the Nobel Prize in 1998.

s: Dashrath Manjhi, known as the Mountain Man, was a labourer from Gehlaur village, near Gaya in Bihar, best known for carving a path through a ridge of hills.
k: Dashrath Manjhi was a poor labourer from a village in Bihar. He cut a path through a rocky hill, and people called him the Mountain Man.

s: Kanshi Ram, also known as Bahujan Nayak, was a politician and social reformer who worked for the uplift and political mobilisation of the Bahujans.
k: Kanshi Ram was a politician and reformer who worked to bring the people called Bahujans into politics.

s: Kamala Surayya, also known as Kamala Das and by the pen name Madhavikutty, was a poet in English and an author in Malayalam from Kerala.
k: Kamala Das was a poet from Kerala who wrote in English and in Malayalam.

s: Tulsi Gowda was an environmentalist from Honnali village who planted more than 30,000 saplings and looked after the nurseries of the Forest Department.
k: Tulsi Gowda planted more than 30,000 young trees in her life.

s: Aruna Roy is a social activist, union organiser and retired officer of the Indian Administrative Service.
k: Aruna Roy is a social activist and union organiser who used to be a government officer.

s: Kiran Bedi is a former tennis player who in 1972 became the first Indian woman to join the officer ranks of the Indian Police Service.
k: In 1972 Kiran Bedi became the first woman officer in the Indian Police Service.

s: Kailash Satyarthi is a social reformer who campaigned against child labour in India and for every child's right to education.
k: Kailash Satyarthi has spent his life working to free children from having to work and to get them into school.

s: Bachendri Pal is a mountaineer, the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest.
k: Bachendri Pal was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest.

s: Medha Patkar is a social activist who works with tribal people, Dalits, farmers, labourers and women facing injustice. She is a founding member of the Narmada Bachao Andolan.
k: Medha Patkar leads people who would lose their homes and land to big dams and other projects.

s: Droupadi Murmu is a politician who has served as President of India since 2022. She is the youngest person to hold the post and the first president born in independent India.
k: Droupadi Murmu became President of India in 2022. She is the first president born after India became free.

s: Jadav "Molai" Payeng, born into the indigenous Mising tribe of Assam, is a forest conservationist from Majuli, popularly known as the Forest Man of India.
k: Jadav Payeng of Assam has spent his life planting a forest. People call him the Forest Man of India.

s: Kalpana Chawla, born at Karnal in Haryana, was an Indian-born American astronaut and aerospace engineer, the first woman of Indian heritage to fly into space. She took part in two spaceflights, in 1997 and 2003.
k: Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal in Haryana. She became an astronaut in America and flew into space twice.

s: Tessy Thomas is an aerospace engineer who worked on India's missile programmes. She joined the Defence Research and Development Organisation in 1985.
k: Tessy Thomas is an engineer who helped to build India's missiles.

s: Phoolan Devi, popularly known as the Bandit Queen, was a dacoit who became a politician, serving as a member of parliament until her assassination.
k: Phoolan Devi was an outlaw who later became a member of parliament. She was killed in 2001.

s: P. T. Usha, born near Perambra in the Kozhikode district of Kerala, is a retired track and field athlete, sports administrator and parliamentarian.
k: P. T. Usha, from a village in Kerala, was one of India's greatest runners.

s: Allah Rakha Rahman is a music composer, record producer, singer and songwriter.
k: A. R. Rahman is a composer, singer and songwriter.

s: Viswanathan "Vishy" Anand is a chess grandmaster and a four-time undisputed World Chess Champion.
k: Viswanathan Anand is a chess grandmaster who became champion of the world.

s: Irom Sharmila Chanu, known as the "Iron Lady of Manipur", is a civil rights activist and poet from the state of Manipur.
k: Irom Sharmila is an activist and poet from Manipur. People call her the Iron Lady of Manipur.

s: Sachin Ramesh Tendulkar is a former international cricketer who captained the Indian national team, widely regarded as one of the greatest cricketers.
k: Sachin Tendulkar is one of the greatest cricketers of all time.

s: Baby Halder is an author whose best-known work is her autobiography, Aalo Aandhari, which describes her harsh life growing up and working as a domestic worker.
k: Baby Halder worked as a servant in other people's homes. She wrote the story of her own hard life, and it became a famous book.

s: Mangte Chungneijang "Mary" Kom is an Olympic boxer, politician and former member of the Rajya Sabha.
k: Mary Kom is a champion boxer who has competed for India at the Olympics.

s: Bhanwari Devi is a social worker from Bhaateri in Rajasthan who was attacked in 1992 by men angered by her efforts to prevent a child marriage. Afterwards women's groups took a case to the Supreme Court.
